meta.title: Domain parameters for the synthetic data engine - Digital Mill Lab (independent concept demo)
meta.purpose: Machine-readable physical, process, logistics, equipment and illustrative economic parameters for the deterministic synthetic data engine. Every row has a source_id (see 'sources') or is explicitly tagged Engineering Assumption / Synthetic Demonstration Data with confidence 'low'.
meta.honesty: These numbers describe a FICTIONAL palm oil mill ('Demo Palm Mill A'). They are public-literature ranges and assumptions, NOT measurements of any company's facility. Synthetic benchmarks are not factory measurements. Prices are illustrative and user-adjustable.

fields.min: lowest plausible (not a hard clamp for scenario episodes)
fields.used_by: module codes: DATA MILL EXEC MAINT LOG ENERGY SCEN ROI TRACE TWIN KPI COPILOT

conventions: Rates are percent of FFB mass (wet) unless the unit says otherwise.
Zone-boundary rows have min = nominal = max (fixed standard values).
Scenario-effect rows are design choices (Synthetic Demonstration Data), not measurements.

sources.title: Krungsri Research - Industry Outlook 2026-2028: Palm Oil Industry
sources.notes: Thai FFB/CPO volumes, OER 18.2% (2025), price levels, B7 biodiesel, stocks, industry capacity utilisation 48.7%.

sources.title: Thongrak, Kongmanee, Kiatpathomchai (PSU) - Oil Palm Development in Thailand: Trends and Progress of Sustainability Efforts (final report for RSPO)
sources.publisher: Prince of Songkla University for RSPO
sources.notes: 149 CPO mills and ~2,274 ramps (2022, DIT); OER 2012-2021 series; ~75-80% of FFB via ramps; special lane in peak season; FFB price series.

sources.title: Elbersen, Meesters, Bakker (Wageningen UR) - Valorization of palm oil (mill) residues
sources.publisher: Wageningen UR Food & Biobased Research / NL Agency
sources.notes: Per t FFB: ~200 kg CPO, 220 kg EFB, 135 kg fibre, 55 kg shell, >600 kg effluent; 17 kWh and ~0.5 t steam per t FFB; boiler eff. 60%; electricity gen. eff. 12%.

sources.title: AOCS Lipid Library - Palm oil
sources.notes: Sterilisation 40 psig for 60-90 min; steam 140-224 kg/t FFB; clarifier 85-90 C, 1-3 h; 0.65 t POME/t FFB; kernel <7% moisture; mills 60-100 t FFB/h.

sources.title: Vijaya, Menon, Sin, Choo (2013) - Residual oil recovery system for a palm oil mill, J. Oil Palm Research 25(1):116-122
sources.publisher: MPOB / Journal of Oil Palm Research
sources.notes: Pressed fibre retains 5-11% oil (dry basis); 0.25-0.55% of FFB; fibre moisture ~36%. Wet-basis conversions in the abstract are internally inconsistent - use dry basis.

sources.title: Univanich Palm Oil PCL - RSPO P&C Public Summary Report (ASA1_2), BSI
sources.notes: Thai mills of 45 and 60 t FFB/h; forecast OER 18.8-20.5% and KER 5.0-5.64%; mills shut down for maintenance and rerouted FFB to another mill.

sources.title: Univanich - Factory & Biogas / news
sources.notes: New Thai mill with initial 60 t FFB/h; biogas engine ~0.95 MW replaced at one mill.

sources.title: Thawornrat et al. (2024) - Correlation between weather conditions and tenera oil palm yield in Surat Thani Province, Rambhai Barni Rajabhat Agricultural Journal 2(2)
sources.publisher: Dept. of Agriculture (Thailand) researchers; Thai journal
sources.notes: 30 palms, age 7-12 y: 261 kg FFB/palm/y, 13.9 bunches, 19.7 kg/bunch; monthly peak Sep 36.19 kg/palm, trough Feb 14.14 kg/palm; monthly rainfall Feb 19.8 mm, Mar 30.1, Apr 70.8, Oct 248.9, Nov 256.1, Dec 317.0. Single site, small sample.

sources.title: Jantaraprasit et al. (2026) - Time-ordered empirical framework for forecasting climate-driven oil palm yield in southern Thailand, Agriculture and Natural Resources 60
sources.notes: Monthly yield (OAE) for 13 southern provinces 2005-2022; yield is lag-sensitive to soil moisture/precipitation; forecast lead 3-20 months; lowest errors in Surat Thani and Nakhon Si Thammarat. Does not print the monthly seasonal profile in text.

sources.title: Putra (2013) - Kinetics of change of free fatty acid and oil content of oil palm due to processing delay, Universitas Sriwijaya (Indonesian thesis)
sources.notes: FFB delay 0-48 h in 8 h steps: FFA 2.96% (0 h) to 5.14% (48 h); oil content not statistically changed; mesocarp moisture fell 30.0% to 18.3%. Single lab study, not mill conditions.

sources.title: Mustaffa, Lau, Choo (2010) - Effect of FFA and oil yield of FFB by prolonging storage after harvesting (AGRIS record)
sources.notes: Qualitative: FFA rises with storage before sterilisation; preliminary data only.

sources.title: Fabrico - ISO 10816-3 vibration severity (zone table); cross-check Beckhoff TF3600 documentation
sources.notes: Fabrico and the usual published table give Group 2 rigid 1.4/2.8/4.5 mm/s; the Beckhoff page lists 3.5 for Group 2 rigid B/C (apparent discrepancy). Standard is superseded by ISO 20816-3 with the same limits. Verify against the licensed standard before any real use.

sources.title: Bearing RTD alarm/trip guidance (TECO-Westinghouse RTD alarm/trip table; GE 469 manual defaults; IEEE C50.13-style presets as quoted by a generator tool)
sources.notes: Only search excerpts read. Rolling bearings commonly alarm 75-90 C, trip 90-100+ C; set from commissioning baseline and OEM rating.

sources.title: Orathai (Chulalongkorn Univ.) - Thai crude palm oil mill thesis, chapter 5 (excerpt)
sources.notes: Search excerpt only (full document could not be opened): 17.11 kWh/t FFB total electricity; 24 h/day x 300 d/yr basis; mills average ~75% of design capacity; most mills energy self-sufficient.

sources.title: Tan et al. (2001) - Palm oil survey for strategic quality improvement and specifications (AGRIS record) plus PORAM/MS 815 excerpts
sources.notes: Confirms CPO is traded on FFA and moisture and impurities. The 5.0% FFA and 0.25% M&I maxima come from search excerpts of PORAM/Malaysian-standard tables (not opened).

sources.title: Emebu et al. (2022) - Influence of moisture content, temperature and time on free fatty acid in stored crude palm oil, Scientific Reports 12:9846
sources.notes: CPO leaves the line at ~90 C and is held 35-55 C; FFA kinetics fit half-order with Arrhenius dependence; quotes low FFA 2-5% and M&I 0.15-0.30%.

sources.title: AGRIS record - Effect of high pressurized sterilization on oil palm fruit digestion operation (digestion at atmospheric pressure, 90-96 C)
sources.notes: Search excerpt only.

sources.title: MPOB Palm Oil Engineering Bulletin 116 - boilers and steam
sources.notes: Excerpt: two 15 t/h boilers at 20 bar were common for a 20 t/h mill; sterilizer steam taken from back-pressure receiver at roughly 1.5-3.5 bar.

parameters.description: Design (nameplate) FFB processing capacity of the fictional demo mill
parameters.notes: 45 and 60 t/h are common Thai design sizes (Univanich mills); a Thai palm oil operator's public RSPO notice lists 60 t/h for its mill (S10) but demo output must NOT be presented as that mill. AOCS quotes 60-100 t/h as general range.

parameters.description: Scheduled running hours per day in a normal-supply day
parameters.notes: A Thai thesis uses 24 h/day x 300 d/yr as design basis; 20 h/day is a common modelling choice (cleaning, shift hand-over, PM). Treat as adjustable.

parameters.description: Operating days per year (excludes annual shutdown and non-running days)
parameters.notes: Thesis design basis 300 d/yr.

parameters.description: Share of design throughput actually achieved over scheduled hours in a normal-supply month
parameters.notes: Thai thesis excerpt: mills average ~75% of design capacity. Industry-wide utilisation is only 48.7% (S13) because Thai capacity exceeds FFB supply - a single well-supplied mill runs higher.

parameters.description: Utilisation in lean-supply months (Feb-Apr)
parameters.notes: Anchored on the 48.7% industry-average utilisation (S13); lean months can be well below average.

parameters.description: Utilisation in peak-supply months (Aug-Oct)
parameters.notes: Peak season produces FFB oversupply, queues and special lanes (S14). Utilisation cannot exceed 1.0 of design for sustained periods; excess FFB waits.

parameters.description: Routine planned stop (cleaning, PM) per week
parameters.notes: No public figure found.

parameters.description: Annual overhaul shutdown
parameters.notes: No public figure found. Univanich report confirms mills do stop for maintenance and reroute FFB (S18).

parameters.description: Unplanned stoppage events per month (plant level, normal period)
parameters.notes: Synthetic rate; no public benchmark.

parameters.description: Mean duration of an unplanned stoppage
parameters.notes: Long-tailed (lognormal) in the generator; max is the 95th percentile.

parameters.description: Scheduled-time mechanical availability of the process line (excludes starvation for lack of FFB)
parameters.notes: Do not count no-FFB stops as downtime.

parameters.description: Average FFB bunch weight (tenera, 7-12 y palms, Surat Thani)
parameters.notes: Annual means 15.56-24.22 kg; monthly bunch weight lowest in Feb (15.68) and highest in Jul (22.08). 30-palm sample.

parameters.description: Thai national FFB yield per harvested rai
parameters.notes: Derived: 21.1 Mt FFB / 6.44 M rai harvested (2025) = 3.28; a Thai palm oil operator site says 3-4 t/rai/yr (S02, S03). 1 ha = 6.25 rai.

parameters.description: Typical ramp/estate-to-mill haul distance
parameters.notes: Smallholder-to-ramp distance averages ~3.6 km (S14 survey); ramp-to-mill leg is longer and unsourced.

parameters.description: Average loaded truck speed on rural roads
parameters.notes: Used with haul distance for transit time.

parameters.description: Industry guidance: time from harvest to sterilisation
parameters.notes: Same-day delivery and processing within ~24 h is the stated practice (AOCS; Krungsri excerpt S44). Above ~48 h quality deteriorates clearly.

parameters.description: Guidance: maximum harvest-to-mill transit time
parameters.notes: Single Indonesian excerpt.

parameters.description: Unripe/underripe bunch share of intake (normal supplier mix)
parameters.notes: No Thai measured figure found; varies strongly by supplier.

parameters.description: Overripe bunch share of intake
parameters.notes: Overripe defined by >5 loose fruit sockets (S40).

parameters.description: Dirt/trash/long-stalk share of ticket weight
Mean grading deduction applied to ticket weight (unripe, long stalk, dirt)
parameters.notes: Mills in Malaysia apply tonnage deductions for poor bunches (S40); exact Thai practice not found.

parameters.description: Oil extraction rate: CPO produced / FFB processed x 100 (nominal mill-level)
parameters.notes: 18.2% = Thai national 2025 (17.7% in 2024). Historic national series 15.85 (2014) to 18.21 (2019) (S14). 20.5% = upper forecast OER used in RSPO mass-balance reports for a Thai mill group (S18), a planning factor not a measured result. Mill-level extremes in the demo (degradation episodes) may go to ~16.0-16.5.

parameters.description: Kernel extraction rate: palm kernel produced / FFB processed x 100
parameters.notes: Univanich KER 5.0-5.64% (forecast and actual); WUR table implies ~6%. Min 4.5 is an assumption for poor kernel recovery.

parameters.description: Empty fruit bunch (EFB) per tonne FFB (wet)
parameters.notes: WUR: ~220 kg per t FFB.

parameters.description: Mesocarp fibre per tonne FFB (wet)
parameters.notes: WUR: ~135 kg per t FFB.

parameters.description: Kernel shell per tonne FFB (wet)
parameters.notes: WUR: ~55 kg per t FFB; max 7.0 is an assumption.

parameters.description: Raw palm oil mill effluent per tonne FFB
parameters.notes: AOCS: 0.65 t/t FFB; WUR: 'more than 600 kg'. Strongly process-dependent (decanter-based mills differ). Do NOT confuse with the other WUR sentence quoting 'm3' on a different basis.

parameters.description: Day-to-day OER measurement/process noise (standard deviation) in normal operation
parameters.notes: Synthetic. Daily OER from tank dips is noisy; weekly averages must be much tighter (~0.10 pp). Do not make OER a smooth constant.

parameters.description: Seasonal swing in OER (peak-supply months higher, lean months lower), half-amplitude
parameters.notes: Direction is supported (bunches riper/larger in peak, S20; CPO production index 76% in Feb vs 120% in Sep/Oct cited by S20 is a production index, not OER). Magnitude is an assumption.

parameters.description: Total oil lost in residues, per FFB mass (normal mill)
parameters.notes: Vendor-quoted average ~1.0%; efficient plants 0.5-0.6%; another vendor figure 0.8-1.5%. Not independent evidence - keep wide.

parameters.description: Oil lost in EFB
parameters.notes: Derived: EFB carries ~0.3-0.4% oil (unverified excerpt) x 22% EFB = ~0.07-0.09% of FFB.

parameters.description: Oil lost in sterilizer condensate
parameters.notes: AOCS wording is ambiguous; ~0.1% of FFB.

parameters.description: Oil lost in pressed fibre/press cake
parameters.notes: Peer-reviewed range 0.25-0.55% of FFB.

parameters.description: Oil lost in clarification sludge/POME
parameters.notes: Vendor average ~0.4%.

parameters.description: Oil lost with nuts, unstripped bunches, decanter cake, spills
parameters.notes: Sum of the five nominal loss terms = 1.00%, equal to oil_loss_total_pct_ffb nominal. Keep the sum consistent.

parameters.description: Residual oil in pressed fibre, dry basis
parameters.notes: Use dry basis; wet-basis numbers in the abstract do not reconcile with 36% moisture.

parameters.description: Moisture of pressed mesocarp fibre
parameters.notes: Average 36% reported.

parameters.description: Sterilizer peak steam pressure (gauge)
parameters.notes: 40 psig = 2.76 bar(g). Triple-peak cycles are staged: ~1.0-1.5 bar first peak, then ~2.8-3.0 bar peaks (staging values are assumptions, see PALM_MILL_PROCESS.md).

parameters.description: Sterilizer cycle time (peak-to-peak cooking, excluding loading)
parameters.notes: AOCS: 60-90 min.

parameters.description: Saturated steam temperature at sterilizer peak
parameters.notes: Physics: saturated steam at ~2.8 bar(g) is ~141 C; Malaysian guidance 130-140 C.

parameters.description: FFB per cage
parameters.notes: AOCS: 2.5-10 t per cage.

parameters.description: Number of horizontal sterilizer vessels in the demo mill
parameters.notes: 5 vessels x 8 cages x 2.5 t = 20 t per vessel per ~100 min => ~60 t/h.

parameters.description: Cages per vessel
Steam used by sterilisation
parameters.notes: AOCS: 140 (single-peak) to 224 (triple-peak). Values above 224 indicate steam leaks or poor cycle control.

parameters.description: Unstripped bunches (oil loss path) after threshing
parameters.notes: Undercooked bunches strip poorly - couples to sterilizer pressure scenario.

parameters.description: Digester mash temperature
parameters.notes: Atmospheric digestion at 90-96 C. Warning below ~85 C or above ~100 C.

parameters.description: Digester residence time
parameters.notes: A patent excerpt cites 20-50 min for pressurised digesters; Thai practice unverified.

parameters.description: Digester vessels
parameters.notes: One per press.

parameters.description: Screw presses
parameters.notes: 6 x 10 t FFB/h = 60 t/h nominal.

parameters.description: Design capacity per screw press
Screw press drive motor rating
parameters.notes: Group 2 machine in ISO 10816-3 terms (15-300 kW).

parameters.description: Press motor current as fraction of full-load current, healthy
parameters.notes: Rises when press wears (cone/screw clearance) or feed is heavy.

parameters.description: Press hydraulic cone/back-pressure setting
parameters.notes: No public number found; model it only as a relative signal. Higher pressure reduces fibre oil loss but raises broken-nut/kernel loss and wear.

parameters.description: Continuous clarification tank temperature
parameters.notes: AOCS 85-90 C; MPOB sources ~90 C. A temperature drop raises sludge oil loss.

parameters.description: Clarifier retention time
parameters.notes: Settling time 1-3 h.

parameters.description: CPO storage tank temperature (held to avoid solidification and oxidation)
parameters.notes: 35-55 C band; loading ~50-55 C; heating ramp <=5 C/24 h unstirred (S41).

parameters.description: CPO density near 50 C
parameters.notes: Standard physical property (not fetched); used to convert tank dips to mass.

parameters.description: Capacity per CPO storage tank
parameters.notes: No public figure.

parameters.description: Number of CPO storage tanks
CPO tanker payload at dispatch
parameters.notes: a Thai terminal operator page quotes 30-32 t payload for its trucks (petroleum/bulk); CPO tanker payload is an assumption.

parameters.description: Free fatty acid of CPO at production (normal supply)
parameters.notes: Literature quotes 2-5% as the quality band. Above 5.0% = off-spec event.

parameters.description: Contractual maximum FFA for crude palm oil
parameters.notes: PORAM/MS style limit; Thai buyers may apply their own contracts.

parameters.description: CPO moisture after vacuum drying
parameters.notes: Combined moisture and impurities cited 0.15-0.30%; split between moisture and dirt is an assumption.

parameters.description: CPO insoluble impurities (dirt)
Contractual maximum moisture and impurities (M&I) in CPO
parameters.notes: moisture + dirt must stay <= 0.25 in normal data; excursions are alerts.

parameters.description: Additional FFA (percentage points) per hour of FFB waiting beyond the free window
parameters.notes: Only one weak lab anchor: 2.96% -> 5.14% over 48 h (mean +0.045 pp/h) for stored bunches, which includes the first hours. S23 and S28 confirm direction only. Never present as measured Thai mill behaviour.

parameters.description: Waiting hours before extra FFA is applied
parameters.notes: Aligned with the ~8 h transit guideline; modelling choice.

parameters.description: FFA drift in warm CPO storage
parameters.notes: S28 shows FFA rises with temperature, moisture and time (Arrhenius, half-order) but the experimental conditions are not mill conditions.

parameters.description: OER reduction per percentage point of unripe bunches above the baseline share
parameters.notes: Direction supported (S40); magnitude assumed. 8 pp extra unripe -> ~0.64 pp OER.

parameters.description: OER reduction per 24 h of FFB delay beyond the 24 h target
parameters.notes: S22 found oil content not statistically changed; weight loss and rot reduce effective OER in practice. Kept small and flagged.

parameters.description: FFB weight loss while waiting in queue/ramp
parameters.notes: S14 notes weight loss in long queues qualitatively; magnitude assumed.

parameters.description: Palm kernel moisture after drying
parameters.notes: Dried to below 7%. AOCS 0.4 t kernel per t CPO is not consistent with Thai OER/KER (KER/OER ~0.29) - use KER.

parameters.description: Total process steam consumption per tonne FFB
parameters.notes: WUR estimate ~0.5; fully insulated best case 0.16 is theoretical.

parameters.description: Boiler operating pressure
parameters.notes: 20 bar was common for older mills (S30); higher in newer plants is an assumption.

parameters.description: Back-pressure receiver / process steam header pressure
parameters.notes: Sterilizer steam from back-pressure receiver at ~1.5-3.5 bar.

parameters.description: Installed boiler capacity (all boilers)
parameters.notes: Full-load demand 60 t/h x 0.5 = 30 t/h plus ~30% margin.

parameters.description: Boiler thermal efficiency on fibre/shell
parameters.notes: WUR assumes 60%.

parameters.description: Overall steam-to-electricity conversion efficiency
parameters.notes: WUR quotes 12%.

parameters.description: Total electricity per tonne FFB (all machines)
parameters.notes: WUR ~17; Thai thesis 17.11 (S26); a slide deck quotes 14-25 (S43).

parameters.description: Installed steam turbine generator
parameters.notes: Average demand at full load = 60 x 17 = 1,020 kW.

parameters.description: Standby diesel genset
parameters.notes: Used for start-up and turbine outages.

parameters.description: Diesel genset specific consumption
parameters.notes: Typical engine range; not mill-specific.

parameters.description: Share of electricity imported from grid
parameters.notes: Most Thai CPO mills are energy self-sufficient (excerpt of S26).

parameters.description: Diesel for loaders/tractors and internal transport
Fresh water intake per tonne FFB
parameters.notes: IOI ~1.4; REA 1.36-1.39; REA internal ceiling <2.5.

parameters.description: Higher heating value of EFB/fibre/shell on dry basis
parameters.notes: WUR: 19 GJ/t dw assumed for all residues.

parameters.description: EFB moisture (fresh weight)
Shell moisture (fresh weight)
POME chemical oxygen demand
parameters.notes: 80,000 mg/L is a design figure in an industry deck; typical lower.

parameters.description: Biogas yield per m3 POME
parameters.notes: 25-30 at 55-60% CH4 and up to 33 at 65% CH4 in design decks; lab studies per kg COD differ.

parameters.description: Methane share of biogas
Electricity per m3 biogas via gas engine
parameters.notes: Derived: 0.6 x 35.8 MJ/m3 = 5.97 kWh thermal x ~35% engine efficiency. A ~0.95 MW biogas engine exists at a Thai mill (S19).

parameters.description: ISO 10816-3 zone boundary A/B, Group 1 machine on rigid support
parameters.notes: Zone A = newly commissioned, B = acceptable long-term, C = restrict operation/plan action, D = damage risk. ISO 10816-3 (superseded by ISO 20816-3, same limits); broadband RMS velocity on bearing housings. Group 1 = >300 kW (or shaft height >315 mm); Group 2 = 15-300 kW (shaft 160-315 mm).

profiles.description: Monthly FFB yield index at one Surat Thani research site (mean = 1.0; Jan..Dec). Anchors: Sep = 36.19/21.75 = 1.66 and Feb = 14.14/21.75 = 0.65 (kg FFB per palm per month vs annual mean 261.01/12). Other months interpolated by the researcher so the mean is exactly 1.0.
profiles.notes: Sourced anchors: Feb (min) and Sep (max). All other months are assumptions informed by monthly rainfall (Feb 19.8, Mar 30.1, Apr 70.8 mm; Oct-Dec >200 mm; other months 100-200 mm). Single site, 30 palms of 7-12 years, 2016-2021. Too peaky for a multi-supplier catchment - use the damped profile for mill intake.

profiles.description: Recommended mill-intake seasonal index: 1 + 0.5 x (site index - 1). Peak-to-trough ratio 1.61, consistent with the ~1.58 ratio implied by a CPO production index of 76% (Feb) vs 120% (Sep/Oct) cited in S20 from Indonesian/Malaysian data.
profiles.notes: Damping factor 0.5 is an assumption. The 120-day demo window (23 Jul - 20 Nov 2026) covers the Aug-Oct peak and the Nov decline - the supply situation where queues and FFB waiting are most plausible. Replace with OAE monthly data (S45) if a real calibration is ever done.

profiles.description: Relative truck arrival intensity by hour of day (00..23), mean = 1.0. Harvest in the morning, deliveries peak late morning to late afternoon, thin at night.

Mild Sunday dip; harvest rounds continue 6-7 days. Thai public holidays are not modelled.

relations.name: Mass balance outputs
relations.formula: cpo_t = ffb_processed_t * oer_pct/100; pk_t = ffb_processed_t * ker_pct/100; efb_t = ffb_processed_t * efb_pct_ffb/100 (same for fibre, shell); pome_t = ffb_processed_t * pome_t_per_t_ffb
relations.note: Outputs are fractions of FFB mass; the remainder (~35%) is water, steam condensate, evaporation and dissolved solids. Do not force outputs to sum to 100% of FFB.

relations.name: Mass plausibility bound
relations.note: Nominal sum 64.4, worst-case upper corner 73.5. A validator should fail anything above 75.

relations.name: Oil loss budget
relations.formula: oil_loss_total_pct_ffb = efb + sterilizer_condensate + fibre + sludge + other; nominal 0.07 + 0.10 + 0.35 + 0.40 + 0.08 = 1.00
relations.note: Extra loss from a scenario (e.g. press degradation) adds to the relevant term.

relations.name: Effective OER
relations.formula: oer_actual = oer_baseline(month) - oer_penalty_pp_per_pp_unripe * max(0, unripe_share - ffb_unripe_share_pct) - oer_penalty_pp_per_24h_delay * max(0, (wait_h + transit_h - 24)/24) - sum(extra_loss_pp from scenarios) + N(0, oer_daily_noise_sd_pp)
relations.note: Apply the production-to-tank lag (3-6 h) when computing daily OER from stock changes; weekly OER is the stable signal.

relations.name: FFB waiting time (Little's law)
relations.note: Link logistics to production: congestion raises ramp stock which raises wait_h which raises FFA via REL-07.

relations.name: Throughput
relations.formula: throughput_t_per_h = mill_capacity_t_ffb_per_h * utilisation(season) * (1 - derate_pct/100) while running; daily_processed_t = sum over running hours; processed <= available FFB (stock + received)
relations.note: Starvation (no FFB) is not equipment downtime.

relations.name: FFA vs delay
relations.formula: cpo_ffa_pct = cpo_ffa_pct_baseline + ffa_rise_pp_per_h_delay * max(0, wait_h + transit_h - ffa_delay_free_hours) + noise
relations.note: Single weak anchor (S22). Cap results at ~8%. FFA > 5.0 raises an off-spec alert.

relations.name: Steam and boiler load
relations.formula: steam_demand_t_per_h = throughput_t_per_h * steam_t_per_t_ffb; boiler_load_fraction = steam_demand_t_per_h / boiler_installed_t_steam_per_h
relations.note: At 60 t/h and 0.5 t/t the demand is 30 t/h = 75% of 40 t/h installed; a +15% energy-efficiency drop pushes it to 86%.

relations.name: Electricity
relations.formula: electrical_kw = throughput_t_per_h * electricity_kwh_per_t_ffb (+ a base load of idle auxiliaries); grid_kwh = electrical_kwh * grid_import_share_of_kwh; diesel_l = genset_kwh * diesel_l_per_kwh

relations.name: Biomass fuel balance
relations.formula: steam enthalpy available = (fibre_dry + shell_dry) * biomass_hhv * 0.85 * boiler_efficiency vs need = steam_t_per_t_ffb * ~2.2 GJ/t
relations.note: Derived from S15 Table 7: fibre 0.091 t dry/t FFB and shell 0.048 t dry/t FFB give ~2.6 GJ HHV/t FFB; with ~0.85 moisture factor and 60% boiler efficiency that is ~1.35 GJ vs ~1.1 GJ steam need => ~20% surplus. A +15% steam increase leaves ~4% surplus, so EFB supplement or shortfall alerts become plausible.

relations.name: POME to biogas to power
relations.formula: pome_m3 = ffb_t * pome_t_per_t_ffb; biogas_m3 = pome_m3 * biogas_m3_per_m3_pome; biogas_kwh_el = biogas_m3 * biogas_kwh_el_per_m3
relations.note: At 60 t/h: 39 m3/h POME => ~1,090 m3/h biogas => ~2.2 MWe potential; only a project, not an installed asset in the demo unless explicitly modelled.

relations.name: CPO stock
relations.formula: stock_close_t = stock_open_t + cpo_produced_t - cpo_dispatched_t; dispatch_trips = ceil(dispatched_t / cpo_tanker_payload_t)
relations.note: OER KPI must use produced = dispatched + stock change.

relations.name: Weighbridge and unloading utilisation
relations.formula: rho_wb = lambda_per_h * weighbridge_events_per_trip * weighbridge_service_min_per_event / 60 / weighbridge_count; rho_unload = lambda_per_h * (payload_t/unloading_rate_t_per_min_per_bay) / 60 / unloading_bays
relations.note: At 5-9 trucks/h rho_wb is ~0.2-0.3, rho_unload ~0.3-0.55; congestion emerges when peak convoys push lambda to 15-25 trucks/h.

relations.name: Vibration health state
relations.formula: zone = A if v < AB, B if v < BC, C if v < CD else D (use the equipment's ISO class); health = Normal (A or B and stable), Warning (C or rising >= X% in 7 d), Critical (D or C with rising trend plus temperature/current corroboration), Maintenance Required (open work order)
relations.note: Computed criteria only; thresholds are parameters above.

relations.name: Illustrative unit economics
relations.formula: revenue_per_t_ffb = oer_pct/100*cpo_price + ker_pct/100*palm_kernel_price; margin = revenue - ffb_price*1000 - processing_cost - maintenance_cost - energy_cost
relations.note: At nominal values: 7,280 + 780 = 8,060 revenue vs 7,500 FFB + 480 conversion/maintenance => ~80 THB/t FFB before energy/by-products. Thin margin is realistic; keep price series mutually consistent.

consistency_checks.rule: oer_pct + ker_pct + efb + fibre + shell <= 75 for every day
daily FFB processed <= capacity * scheduled hours; excess FFB waits on the ramp (no instantaneous processing above design)
CPO stock never negative; produced = dispatched + delta stock within rounding
sum of oil-loss terms equals the stated total each day (within rounding)
steam per t FFB in 0.35-0.80 and electricity 12-30 kWh/t for any day with throughput > 20 t/h
FFB mean waiting time equals ramp stock / throughput within 15%
truck net weight = gross - tare >= 0 and <= class payload max * 1.15; flag, do not accuse, outliers
FFA between 1.5 and 8; moisture+dirt between 0.05 and 0.6; clarifier temp 70-98; digester 80-102
vibration health state must be derivable from the stored readings and the ISO thresholds
seasonal index applied to supply means monthly mean intake ratio stays within +/-10% of the profile over a full month window
